open_points.subject: caller-supplied content identities
open_points.text: “A request that supplies one of these identities is refused.” Flow composition and other requests must legitimately name existing contract_version_id, implementation_id, flow_version_id or value_id records.
open_points.question: Is the prohibition limited to supplying the identity of the new content record being created, or does it apply to every occurrence of these identity fields in a request?
options: Refuse only an asserted identity for the content record being created
Refuse any occurrence of a listed identity
Define a per-operation list of identities that may be references
open_points.default_guess: Refuse only an asserted identity for the content record being created; allow identities used to reference existing records.

open_points.subject: contract validation precedence
open_points.text: A16 validates the operation schema before operation-specific checks, while A02 orders conditions such as positive integer bounds, media-type presence and output presence without saying which are schema constraints.
open_points.question: Which A02 conditions are enforced by the surface schema and which are operation checks, so that the first refusal is deterministic?
options: Schema checks only structural field types and A02 performs all listed semantic checks
Put every expressible A02 condition in the schema
Specify the allocation condition by condition
open_points.default_guess: Use the schema for basic shape and primitive types only, then apply every A02 condition in its stated order.

open_points.subject: function determinism
open_points.text: The sandbox traps the listed clock and randomness APIs, but the required test says “The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.” Standard-library code can still observe varying state through APIs such as process identifiers, filesystem metadata or unlisted clock functions.
open_points.question: Must the sandbox prevent every observable nondeterministic source, or is deterministic output merely an unenforced requirement on implementations?
options: Trap or virtualize every nondeterministic observable
Permit unlisted observables and do not guarantee repeatability
Run executions more than once and refuse differing results
open_points.default_guess: Treat determinism as an enforced sandbox property and trap or virtualize other varying observables.

open_points.subject: clock prohibition
open_points.text: K-02 says a function has “no clock”, while A03 says the replaced clock entry points are “exactly” its closed list, which omits other CPython clock-bearing APIs such as time.clock_gettime and filesystem timestamps.
open_points.question: Are unlisted ways of reading time intentionally usable, or must all clock-bearing APIs be unavailable despite the closed list?
options: Only the listed calls are prohibited and other time observations are allowed
All clock observations are prohibited and the release list must cover them
Expose deterministic virtual time for otherwise unlisted APIs
open_points.default_guess: Prohibit all clock observations and expand the release-controlled traps or isolation accordingly.

open_points.subject: sandbox stdout and stderr
open_points.text: “Nothing the code prints or raises is interpreted by the kernel” and “never stdout” do not state whether stdout and stderr are inherited, discarded, piped, or bounded.
open_points.question: How are stdout and stderr connected, and what outcome results when code writes an unbounded amount to them?
options: Redirect both to a bounded sink and classify excess as resource_exhausted
Discard both directly without counting them
Pipe them while retaining no content
Inherit host streams
open_points.default_guess: Redirect both to a bounded discard sink and classify excess as resource_exhausted.

open_points.subject: sandbox scratch accounting
open_points.text: The exchange directory is “bounded by sandbox_scratch_bytes_max”, but the text does not say whether inputs placed there, outputs, temporary files, or all of them consume the bound.
open_points.question: Exactly which bytes count toward sandbox_scratch_bytes_max, when is the check made, and how is an input set already larger than the bound classified?
options: Count all files in the exchange directory, including staged inputs
Count only files created or enlarged by user code
Count only output files
open_points.default_guess: Count all bytes in the exchange directory, including staged inputs, and classify an overage as resource_exhausted.

open_points.subject: resource-exhaustion detection
open_points.text: The first “limit hit” must be resource_exhausted, while an abnormal process exit is crashed, but the rules do not define how the parent distinguishes an exit caused by memory, process or scratch limits from another signal or abnormal exit.
open_points.question: What observable evidence conclusively classifies a terminated sandbox as resource_exhausted rather than crashed?
options: Define per-limit supervisor signals and accounting evidence
Classify specified operating-system signals as resource_exhausted
Classify any unconfirmed limit-related termination as crashed
open_points.default_guess: Require explicit supervisor accounting for a limit hit; otherwise classify the abnormal exit as crashed.

open_points.subject: trial-case input and expected-output shape
open_points.text: A case is added when its inputs “fit the contract version's input ports” and expected outputs “fit the output ports”, but exact presence, absence of extra names, and whether expected_outputs must contain every output are not stated.
open_points.question: Must trial inputs contain exactly every input port and no others, and, when expected_outputs is present, must it contain exactly every output port?
options: Both maps must be exact
Inputs are exact but expected outputs may be partial
Both maps may be partial
Missing entries have an explicit wildcard meaning
open_points.default_guess: Require exact inputs and, when expected_outputs is present, exact outputs.

open_points.subject: rollback eligibility
open_points.text: Rollback selects “an earlier implementation” with a current-corpus admitted verdict, but “earlier” is not defined.
open_points.question: Must a rollback target have previously been active, merely have been submitted before the current implementation, or may any existing admitted implementation be selected?
options: Only a previously active implementation
Any implementation submitted before the current one
Any implementation with an admitted current-corpus verdict
open_points.default_guess: Allow any existing implementation of the current contract version with an admitted verdict over the current corpus.

open_points.subject: connection concurrency
open_points.text: The preamble says “no concurrent connections”, while A18 only says requests are handled one at a time.
open_points.question: Must a second simultaneous MCP connection be rejected, or may multiple connections remain open while their requests are serialized?
options: Reject concurrent connections
Allow concurrent connections but serialize requests
Permit only one in-flight request regardless of connection count
open_points.default_guess: Allow multiple connections but permit only one in-flight request.

open_points.subject: token-list configuration reread
open_points.text: A17 requires the configuration file to be regular, non-symlinked, owner-owned and private, but A16's later reread applies “Exactly four checks” that omit ownership, mode and symlink checks.
open_points.question: Must every token-list reread revalidate the configuration file's ownership, permissions and non-symlink status?
options: Repeat all A17 file-security checks on every reread
Apply those checks only at startup
Keep an already-open file descriptor and reread only that object
open_points.default_guess: Repeat all A17 file-security checks on every reread before accepting the new token list.

open_points.subject: surface request byte count
open_points.text: Request size is “the bytes of the request message as received”, without defining whether this is MCP framing, serialized JSON, decoded operation arguments, or another representation.
open_points.question: Which exact byte sequence is measured against surface_request_bytes_max?
options: The complete serialized MCP message before decoding
Only the serialized operation arguments
The transport frame including protocol framing
A canonical re-encoding after decoding
open_points.default_guess: Measure the complete serialized MCP request message payload before decoding, excluding transport framing.

open_points.subject: credential text normalization
open_points.text: A secret is decoded as UTF-8 “without one trailing newline” and rejected if it “holds ... a control character”, but newline form and the control-character set are not defined.
open_points.question: Is the removable newline LF only or CRLF as well, are multiple trailing newlines rejected or partly stripped, and which Unicode code points count as control characters?
options: Strip exactly one LF, then reject all remaining Unicode control characters
Strip one LF or one CRLF, then reject C0, DEL and C1 controls
Trim all trailing line endings, then validate
open_points.default_guess: Strip exactly one terminal LF or CRLF and reject any remaining C0, DEL or C1 control character.

open_points.subject: data-directory privacy check
open_points.text: “The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user” does not define acceptable owners, permission bits, ACLs, hard links, or file types.
open_points.question: What exact filesystem conditions satisfy “private”, both at startup and for newly created files?
options: Require kernel ownership and no group/other permission bits
Also reject ACL access, hard links and unexpected file types
Rely only on directory permissions
open_points.default_guess: Require kernel-user ownership, no group/other permissions, no granting ACLs, and only expected regular files or directories.

open_points.subject: concurrent request arrival order
open_points.text: Requests are handled “one at a time in the order they arrive”, but simultaneous arrival across MCP connections has no defined ordering point.
open_points.question: What event establishes the total arrival order used for request execution and store order?
options: Order when a full request has been decoded
Order when the first transport byte arrives
Order by a single listener queue sequence number
Reject overlap so ties cannot occur
open_points.default_guess: Assign a monotonically increasing sequence when a complete request enters the single dispatcher queue.

open_points.subject: unreferenced spool files
open_points.text: A failed store call may leave “a published file no record names”, and startup removes only temporary files and spool directories of ended runs; A13 also leaves failed-attempt files in an active run's spool.
open_points.question: Are unreferenced published spool files removed on restart, and do they count toward spool_run_bytes_max before removal?
options: Remove all unreferenced spool files during recovery and count them until removed
Keep them until the run ends and count them
Keep them but exclude them from the quota
Remove them immediately after a failed store call
open_points.default_guess: Count them while present and remove every unreferenced spool file during startup recovery.

open_points.subject: durability before external effects
open_points.text: The rules require the in-flight EffectAttempt to be in the store before sending, but “one transaction” does not specify when a successful store call is durable against process or power loss.
open_points.question: What durability guarantee and SQLite synchronization settings are required before an HTTP effect may be sent or a surface success returned?
options: The transaction must be durably committed and fsynced before proceeding
Process-crash durability is required but power-loss durability is not
A logical SQLite commit is sufficient regardless of filesystem persistence
open_points.default_guess: Require a durably committed transaction, including the necessary database and directory synchronization, before sending an effect.

open_points.subject: bubblewrap dependency pin
open_points.text: A20 says one release fixes “every dependency”, but A03 only checks that bubblewrap is present and a probe succeeds; no bubblewrap version or build is pinned.
open_points.question: Is bubblewrap part of the pinned release dependency set, and if so what exact version or compatibility identity must startup verify?
options: Pin and verify an exact bubblewrap version/build
Define and probe a supported version range
Treat bubblewrap as an unpinned host prerequisite
open_points.default_guess: Pin a supported bubblewrap version and verify it at startup.

open_points.subject: ceiling changes across releases
open_points.text: Rule 4 grandfathers only earlier contract bounds; it does not say how reduced ceilings apply to existing implementation code, StoredValues, trial fixtures, run spools, or cached responses created under an earlier release.
open_points.question: Which old records and artifacts remain usable when a new release lowers their corresponding global ceiling?
options: Grandfather every already-stored artifact and apply new ceilings only to new writes
Grandfather only contract bounds and refuse operations that encounter oversized old artifacts
Refuse startup until oversized artifacts are migrated or removed
Specify behavior separately for every ceiling
open_points.default_guess: Grandfather existing immutable artifacts, while applying the new ceilings to new requests, writes and executions except for explicitly preserved contract resource bounds.

open_points.subject: security-review completeness gate
open_points.text: The invariant requires “every_required_category_has_one_outcome”, but no authoritative set or derivation rule for required security categories is defined.
open_points.question: What closed list or deterministic procedure decides which security-review categories are required, so the completeness claim can be checked without trusting the review itself?
options: Define a closed required-category enumeration
Derive categories mechanically from declared actors and boundaries
Treat the categories shown in A21 as the complete required set
open_points.default_guess: Declare the categories listed in A21 as a closed required enumeration for State 2.

open_points.subject: flow activation pinned by a run
open_points.text: A10 and M26 require a draft-write EffectAttempt to name “the flow activation under which the run started”, but M19 and A12 pin only flow_version_id and function implementations, not the FlowActivation record's store position.
open_points.question: Where is the exact FlowActivation identity for a run stored or deterministically recoverable, especially after the same version is activated again?
options: Add the FlowActivation store position to Run
Store it only on each draft-write EffectAttempt when first reached
Infer the latest matching activation before run creation from store order
open_points.default_guess: Pin and store the exact FlowActivation position on the Run at creation.

open_points.subject: empty mapped file output
open_points.text: An empty mapped node writes one NodeExecution with “every output an empty list” and says the empty list is “named” by that record, but M23 can name file outputs only through SpooledFile facts and an empty file list has no SpooledFile; M21 forbids run files from being StoredValues.
open_points.question: How does a NodeExecution represent an empty many-file output durably?
options: Add an explicit empty file-list reference/value form
Permit a run-time StoredValue representing only the empty file list
Represent it as an empty list directly in NodeExecution despite the no-payload rule
Infer it solely from the mapped-empty status and port declaration
open_points.default_guess: Represent it by an explicit typed empty-file-list marker in the NodeExecution.

open_points.subject: records used to continue a run
open_points.text: “The trace is the only source the kernel uses to explain or continue a run,” while A10, A11 and A14 require approvals, grants, EffectAttempts, WaitingPoints and Run state in addition to NodeExecution trace records.
open_points.question: Does “trace” include all of those authority and run records, or is rule 7 intended only to exclude process logs?
options: Define trace broadly to include every durable run-related record
Change the rule to say durable store records, not only the trace
Use NodeExecutions alone and derive all other state from them
open_points.default_guess: Interpret the rule as saying all durable kernel records are authoritative and process logs are never authoritative.

open_points.subject: manifest document schema
open_points.text: Rule 5 checks selected missing or invalid fields but does not define the complete types and shapes of service, capabilities, capability names, exposed_as, idempotency_key, instances or required_headers.
open_points.question: What complete manifest schema is validated, and where in rule 5's first-failure order do type and shape errors occur?
options: Define a closed manifest JSON schema and a fixed validation order
Treat any unlisted shape problem as invalid JSON
Accept extra and weakly typed shapes wherever listed checks can operate
open_points.default_guess: Define a closed manifest schema and place each structural failure immediately before the semantic check that consumes that field.

open_points.subject: binding-port validation order
open_points.text: Rule 5 checks key fields and A09 request shape before checking duplicate port names, even though those earlier checks must resolve ports by name.
open_points.question: When duplicate same-direction port names exist, which duplicate is used by key-field and request-shape checks, or must uniqueness be checked first despite the stated order?
options: Move unique-name validation before every name lookup
Use the first duplicate in request order
Evaluate all duplicates and require all to satisfy the earlier check
Refuse duplicates only at the later listed check
open_points.default_guess: Check unique port names before any key-field or request-shape lookup.

open_points.subject: binding port rules inherited from A02
open_points.text: A binding is refused when “its ports break a rule A02 sets for contract ports — unique names per direction, a media type exactly on file ports — or leave out the class M01 requires”, but A02 also requires supported schemas and prohibits classes on contract outputs, whereas bindings require output classes.
open_points.question: Exactly which A02 port rules apply to binding ports, including schema-subset, cardinality and disclosure-class rules?
options: Only the two rules explicitly named between dashes apply
All A02 port rules apply except the contract-output class rule
Define a separate complete binding-port validation list
open_points.default_guess: Define a separate complete list: supported schema, valid direction/cardinality/carriage, unique names, media type exactly on files, and disclosure class on every binding input and output.

open_points.subject: configured manifest revision semantics
open_points.text: The kernel reads files “at the configured manifest_revision”, but no mechanism defines how a filesystem location is resolved at a repository revision or what happens when that revision is invalid or mutable.
open_points.question: How is manifest_revision resolved and verified, and what exact failure results when the revision cannot be read?
options: The kernel reads a Git object/tree at that exact commit
The host provides an immutable checkout and the revision is informational
The kernel verifies that the working tree currently matches the configured revision
open_points.default_guess: Read manifest files directly from the exact immutable repository commit identified by manifest_revision.

open_points.subject: manifest mutation during a running kernel
open_points.text: Rule 6 rereads the operation before every send, while it also says “a record changes for a running kernel only after a restart with a new configured revision.” Nothing states that files at the configured location and revision cannot change in place.
open_points.question: Must the kernel enforce immutability of the configured revision, or can an in-place manifest edit change send behavior before restart?
options: Resolve every read from an immutable revision object
Permit in-place changes and let rule 6 detect them immediately
Cache the manifest at startup and never reread files until restart
open_points.default_guess: Resolve every manifest read from an immutable revision object so in-place working-tree changes are irrelevant.

open_points.subject: base URL validity and joining
open_points.text: A08 accepts any absolute http or https URL with a host, while A09 concatenates the base URL without a trailing slash and the declared path; query, fragment, user-info and non-root base paths are not addressed.
open_points.question: Which components may api_base_url contain, and how are a base path, percent escapes, user-info, query or fragment handled?
options: Allow only scheme, host and optional port with no path, query, fragment or user-info
Allow a base path and define RFC-compliant path joining
Use literal string concatenation for every otherwise-valid absolute URL
open_points.default_guess: Allow only scheme, host and optional port, with no user-info, query, fragment or non-root path.

open_points.subject: empty path-placeholder value
open_points.text: A path placeholder accepts any non-null string or integer, but an empty string does not remain one path segment and can create a double slash.
open_points.question: Is an empty string valid for a path placeholder, and if not, which pre-send refusal does it produce?
options: Refuse an empty path value as input_cannot_be_placed
Encode it as an empty segment
Introduce an explicit encoding for an empty segment
open_points.default_guess: Refuse it before sending as an input that cannot be placed in the request.

open_points.subject: multipart field-name and filename encoding
open_points.text: Multipart headers interpolate the unrestricted port name into name="<port>" and filename="<port>" without defining escaping or restricting quotes, backslashes, CR, LF or non-ASCII characters.
open_points.question: What port-name syntax or escaping algorithm makes multipart Content-Disposition headers unambiguous and injection-safe?
options: Restrict multipart-used port names to a safe ASCII token subset
Escape quoted-string characters and reject CR/LF
Use RFC 5987-style extended parameters for non-ASCII names
open_points.default_guess: Reject CR/LF and restrict port names used in multipart parameters to a conservative ASCII identifier syntax.

open_points.subject: response content encoding
open_points.text: The kernel sends Accept-Encoding: identity, but the rules do not say what happens if a service nevertheless returns Content-Encoding such as gzip.
open_points.question: Is an encoded response rejected, decoded before size and credential checks, or treated as opaque bytes?
options: Reject any non-identity Content-Encoding as contract_violation
Decode supported encodings and count decoded bytes
Treat encoded bytes as the response body without decoding
open_points.default_guess: Reject any non-identity content encoding as contract_violation.

open_points.subject: incomplete body after final status
open_points.text: The table classifies reset or EOF with “no valid final response” before classifying 3xx, 4xx and 5xx statuses, but does not say whether a final status with an incomplete or malformed body is already a valid final response.
open_points.question: For each status class, what outcome applies when final headers arrive but the framed body times out, resets or ends prematurely?
options: Treat every incomplete framed body as no valid final response
Let 3xx, 4xx and 5xx status alone determine the outcome, but require a complete body for 2xx
Let any final status determine the outcome regardless of body completion
open_points.default_guess: Treat an incomplete framed body as no valid final response; for non-read effects the outcome is unknown.

open_points.subject: standing-grant request validation
open_points.text: A grant is given for “a node of the flow's active version whose effect class is not destructive”, but the checks for flow/version/node existence, node kind, binding status, active-version match, effect class and an already-active grant are not ordered.
open_points.question: What exact checks and precedence govern grant and revoke requests, including a function node or a node whose binding is no longer accepted?
options: Define a complete fixed check order for grant and revoke
Rely on generic unknown-reference checks followed by the sentence's order
Allow grants only for operation nodes and otherwise use one generic refusal
open_points.default_guess: After generic reference checks, verify operation-node kind, active-version match, non-destructive class, then return an existing active grant or create one; define revoke analogously.

open_points.subject: meaning and mutability of trace records
open_points.text: A01 says no “trace record” is edited, A15 makes NodeExecution immutable, while M26 and A11 mutate EffectAttempt from in_flight to an outcome and from unknown to a resolution; A14 also rewrites Run status and WaitingPoints.
open_points.question: Which record types are members of the immutable trace, and which are mutable run or authority state outside it?
options: Only NodeExecution is an immutable trace record
NodeExecution and EffectAttempt are trace records, requiring append-only replacement events
All run-related records are trace records and must become append-only
open_points.default_guess: Define NodeExecution as the immutable trace record; treat Run, WaitingPoint, EffectApproval and EffectAttempt as separately governed mutable state.
